<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|157}}</noinclude>Iohns baptisme. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=30}}† But the Pharisees and the lavvyers {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ As they that contēned Iohns baptisme, despised Gods counsel and wisedō: so much more they that make no accoumpt of the Sacraments of the Church, despise Gods counsel and ordinance touching their saluation, to their owne damnation.}}∷ despised the counsel of God against them selues, being not baptized of him. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=31}}† And our Lord said, VVherevnto then shal I liken the men of this generation, and vvherevnto are they like? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=32}}† They are like to children sitting in the market-place, and speaking one to an other, and saying, VVe haue piped to you, and you haue not daunced: vve haue lamented, and you haue not vvept. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=33}}† For Iohn the Baptist came {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 4.''}}* neither eating bread nor drinking vvine: and you say, He hath a deuil. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=34}}† The sonne of man came eating and drinking: and you say, Behold a man that is a gurmander and a drinker of vvine, a frende of Publicans and sinners. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=35}}† And vvisedom is iustified of al her children.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=36}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō S. Marie Magdalens day Iul. 22. And vpon Thursday in Passion weeke. And vpō Imber Friday in Sept.}}And one of the Pharisees desired him to eate vvith him. And being entred into the house of the Pharisee, he sate downe to meate. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=37}}† And behold a vvoman that was in the citie, a sinner, as she knevv that he vvas set downe in the Pharisees house, she brought an alabaster boxe of ointment: {{verse|chapter=7|verse=38}}† and standing behind beside his feete, she began to {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ A perfect paterne of true penance in this vvoman, who sought of Christ with open teares & other strange workes of satisfaction and deuotion, remission of her sinnes.}}∷ vvater his feete vvith teares, & vviped them vvith the heares of her head, and kissed his feete, & anointed them with the ointment. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=39}}† And the Pharisee that had bid him, seeing it, spake vvithin him self, saying, This man if he vvere a Prophet, vvould know certes vvho and vvhat maner of woman she is vvhich toucheth him, that she is a sinner. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=40}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} answering said to him, Simon, I haue somevvhat to say vnto thee. but he said, Maister, say. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=41}}† A certaine creditour had tvvo debters: one did ovve fiue hundred pence, and the other fiftie. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=42}}† They hauing not vvherevvith to pay, he forgaue both. VVhether therfore doth loue him more? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=43}}† Simon ansvvering said, I suppose that he to vvhom he forgaue more. But he said to him, Thou hast iudged rightly. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=44}}† And turning to the vvoman, he said vnto Simon, Doest thou see this vvoman? I entred {{sup|‖}} into thy house, vvater to my feete thou didst not giue: but she vvith teares hath vvatered my feete, and vvith her heares hath vviped them. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=45}}† Kisse thou gauest me not: but she since I came in, hath not ceased to kisse my feete. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=46}}† VVith oile thou didst not anoint my head: but she vvith ointment hath anointed my feete. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=47}}† For the vvhich I say to thee, Many sinnes are forgiuen her, because she hath {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not only faith (as you may perceiue) but loue or charitie obtaineth remission of sinnes.}}∷ loued much. But to vvhom lesse is forgiuen, he loueth lesse. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=48}}† And he said to her, Thy sinnes are forgiuen<noinclude>{{rh||V iij|thee.}}</noinclude>
